LowGpuFile.description:
The low-GPU voice profile: while something else needs the GPU (a game, another job), the voice helper starts with a lighter set of models, the setup assistant's light tier (voice-models.ts recommendedChoices) among the models already here: Parakeet only (no Whisper reading again), Pocket TTS reading on the CPU, else Kokoro (no Qwen3-TTS), the speaker and turn models, which run on the CPU. voice.json is never written: the set is put over it (configPatch) on the configuration the helper starts with.

It is on while a holder holds it (`roamgate voice profile low-gpu on
--by <name>`, the settings' switch) or GameMode runs as a call starts. The holders are kept in the voice's data directory (lowGpuPath): the CLI writes them there, the server watches the file. A helper running with the other set stops once nothing needs it (a call ending), the next request starting it with the right one; `--now` restarts it at once, its call made again after a short notice.

On for a game (the "gaming" holder, GameMode), the helper also yields the CPU to it (yieldCpu): a low priority and CPU weight, idle I/O, and its ONNX models (Parakeet, Kokoro, the speaker and turn checks) sharing a few threads that do not spin, where each would otherwise take one per core, and Pocket TTS computing on as few, its workers parking between steps: a game freezes when the voice takes the cores it runs on.

rejected.description: Upstream commits said not to be this one: never proposed again.

SshForwardDirection.description:
Which way the tunnel runs.

`local` (ssh -L) puts a remote service on a local port: the browser reaches something running on the far host. `remote` (ssh -R) is the mirror, a service on this machine appears on the far host, so processes there, agents included, can reach it.

The trust story is not symmetric. A local forward exposes the far host's service to this machine alone; a remote forward exposes ours to everything on the far host. Both ask for loopback, which is the only reason the second is reasonable at all; see sshForwardArgv for where the far host can override that.

groups.description: From the top-level group to the nearest.

It keeps what the lease said of the session and gives it back with its `fg` (Roamgate keeps no lease meanwhile).

title.description: Herdr-rendered text; status-derived events leave these unset.

tried.description: When a refresh was last tried, whatever came of it.

missing.description: The parts Spotify did not give the last time, and why.

needs_login.description: Spotify asked to log in again (403): the user must re-authorize.

avoid.description: What was turned down: a URI or search words, and when.

picks.description: The last picks of open requests, the newest last.

genres.description: Genres from the top artists, the heaviest first (weights 0-100).

anchors.description: Top tracks of the last weeks and months.

playlists.description: The user's own playlists, then followed ones.

contexts.description: Playlists, albums and artists played lately, the most played first.

recent.description: The last days' plays, the newest first.

hours.description: Hours (local, 0-23) most played at, the most first.

recorder_running.description: False when the recorder is not running: open spans end at its last stamp.

gaps.description: The schema's RecordingGap, clipped to the day; `end` null while open.

TimelineSource.description: browser and phone are Roamgate clients; herdr is Herdr's TUI focus.

bytes.description: On `audio`: how much came, as 16 kHz mono S16LE.

pause_ms.description: On a partial at a pause: how far into it the words were read, whether the speaker sounds to be thinking ("euh"), and at speechgate's checks, how finished the voice (`turn`) and the words (`words`) sound, 0 to 1.

raw.description: On a cleaned final: the words as heard, and whether to the agent.

voice.description: On a final, with a speaker model: whose voice (voice-speakers.ts).

voice_label.description: On a final relayed to a page: the voice's label for the companion.

recoverable.description: On a session's `error`: the helper stopped under it, and runs again from the next request. The session is over, nothing else is.

VoiceEvent.description: What the helper says about a listening session.

voices.description: The set of voices its names belong to: a new one each call.

id.description: The voice most heard, null when too little was heard to tell.

share.description: That voice's share of the utterance's voice, 0 to 1.

mix.description: Each voice heard and its share, the most heard first.

similarity.description: How close the utterance is to each voice known, -1 to 1.

merged.description: Voices found to be one: gone name to kept name.

print.description: The utterance's print (the helper's; not sent on to the page).

prints.description: The print of each voice in it (likewise).

utterance.description: Which utterance it is, for its print kept here (observe()).

VoiceTag.description: What the helper says of an utterance's voices (a final's `voice`).

herdr_ms.description: Herdr's TUI focus, only where no browser or phone had attention and within `idle_seconds` of a sign of a person.

working_ms.description: Time at least one of the workspace's agents was working.
